newsitem.title: UK: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week in Review.
newsitem.headline: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week in Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week July 18 to July 25, 1997
**JULY 18**

HONG KONG - A seventh round of talks between the Airport Authority and airline representatives ended with airlines still not knowing how much they will have to pay to use Hong Kong's new airport due to open in nine months time, airline sources said.
HONG KONG - A planned bridge linking Hong Kong with the western Pearl River delta could have major long term implications for Hong Kong's freight industry experts said.
LONDON - The Antonov Design Bureau Genoa airport strongly criticised Genoa airport for not doing enough to resolve a serious bird infestation problem.
BONN - German Chancellor Helmut Kohl urged European aerospace firms to consolidate in response to the competitive threat from the planned merger of Boeing with McDonnell Douglas.
LONDON - TIACA said exhibit space at its 19th International Air Cargo Forum and Exposition in Paris, May 3-6, 1998, is nearly 50 percent booked.
LONDON - BA said it signed a memorandum of understanding committing it to discussing a co-operation deal with Iberia.
MADRID - Iberia said it reached a preliminary agreement on a co-operation deal with BA.
NEWARK - Kiwi International Air Lines said the sale of its assets to Kiwi International Holdings for about $16.5 million was approved in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Newark, N.J.
BRUSSELS - Ostend Airport said it called for a level playing field in Europe on the operating rules for old and noisy Chapter 2 aircraft.
MOSCOW - Russian cargo airline AO Volga-Dnepr delivered from London to Tunisia 100 tonnes of equipment for shooting George Lucas' new Star Wars film, a company spokesman said.
MOSCOW - Aeroflot starts daily scheduled flights between Moscow and Vladivostok from July 29, a company spokesman said.
LONDON - AirRep said it organised an Ilyushin IL-76 freighter flight from Oslo to Pyongyang, North Korea, carrying 42 tonnes of protein foodstuffs.
AMSTERDAM - Aalsmeer flower auction said it is concerned about the effect a night ban on certain wide-body aircraft would have on its flower imports at Amsterdam Schiphol Airport.
LONDON - BA Cargo operations are 90 pct back to normal after disruption caused by last week's 72-hour cabin crew strike, said its regional manager Europe Dennis Connolly.
NEW YORK - Mercury Air said it has taken a minority stake in Patriot Aviation Services.
LUXEMBOURG - Cargolux said it flew 186.1 million FTK's, last month, up 14 pct on June 1996.
BUENOS AIRES - American Airlines will buy 10 pct of the holding company of Aerolineas Argentinas in a deal signed by American and Aerolineas's operator, Iberia , Aerolineas said.
MADRID - Spain said Iberia signed key alliances in Europe and N.America.
DULLES - Atlantic Coast Airlines said its increasing its service to three cities from September 9.
NEW YORK - UAL flight attendants will get raises and bonus totalling 36 pct over the next 10 years, part of a tentative labour agreement reached earlier this week, the union said.

HOUSTON - Continental said it will ask the U.S. Department of Transportation to closely scrutinise the proposed alliance of American Airlines and BA in light of their pending marketing relationship with Iberia
**JULY 19**
BOMBAY - Air India and SIA reached an agreement on additional traffic rights, Air India said.
**JULY 20**
HAMBURG - The president of Germany's Federal Cartel Office reaffirmed European opposition to the proposed $14 bln merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.
**21 JULY **
MINNEAPOLIS/ST. PAUL - Northwest Airlines said it exercised previously announced options for the acquisition of twenty-four British Aerospace Avro RJ85 regional jet aircraft.

HONG KONG - The chairman of the Hong Kong Shippers' Council, Chan Wing Kee, said Hong Kong is liable to price itself out of the market if charges at Chek Lap Kok airport are not kept within users' ability to pay.
DUBAI - Sharjah airport said cargo volumes rose 26 pct in June compared to same month last year.
LONDON - BA said it invited BASSA, its biggest cabin crew union, to meet to table union proposals on how to achieve the 42 million stg ($70.5 million) savings wanted in a pay restructuring dispute.
HONG KONG - China Southern Airlines intends to offer up to 500 million A-shares to Chinese investors subject to approval by relevant authorities, the airline operator said.
LONDON - The number of passengers passing through British airports is expected to grow by between 15 and 27 pct by the year 2001/02 compared with 1996/97, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) said.
MADRID - Spain's Industry Minister Josep Pique said the government was aiming to float around 50 pct of Iberia by the end of 1999, local agency Europa Press reported.
AMSTERDAM - KLM and Oman Air formed a code-sharing agreement, effective from August 1, a KLM spokesman said.
SEATTLE - Alaska Air said it expects the year-over-year results of its unit, Horizon Air Industries to begin to stabilise in Q3 and become positive as its fleet transition is completed.
SEATTLE - Boeing said jet aircraft deliveries for the year are currently projected to be in the 340-350 range.
GENEVA - An unidentified person was killed in a shooting incident at Geneva's Cointrin international airport, police said.
LONDON - BAA said it has appointed John Speakman as general manager cargo, with effect from September 1.
ROME - DHL said it signed an agreement with Femar spa, Catania for transporting cargo and documents.
DAR ES SALAAM - Alliance Air will add an extra direct flight between Tanzania and London from the beginning of next month, a senior manager for the airline said.
